title: Benchmark experiment
description: What to sweep: which images, which apps, which rank/thread decompositions, and how the cross product is split into jobs. Host-side only -- bench/submit expands this into a flat job.env per job, and the job itself never parses YAML.

schema.description: Format version of this file. Bumped only for a change that an older bench/submit would misread.

account.description: Scheduler project to charge. --account overrides it; there is deliberately no default, because this is a billable allocation.

defaults.description: Job-level settings. Anything an app does not override itself.

repeats.description: Times each cell is run. Reported as min and median, never as a single sample.

scale.description: BENCH_SCALE: an app-defined size class (smoke, node, weak, strong).

exclusive.description: Ask the scheduler for every core on each node, whether or not the cells use them all. True by default, and for a benchmark that is the only defensible setting: a co-tenant's work on the same node lands in your timings as noise you cannot see or subtract. Set it false only on a machine whose nodes are shared by design -- Casper's high-throughput nodes -- where holding a whole node means a long wait to drain other people's small jobs. Then the job requests exactly what its cells use, schedules in minutes, and produces numbers that verify the harness rather than measure the hardware.

allow_undersubscribed.description: Permit a ranks x threads product that leaves cores idle. Off by default: --cpu-bind depth packs consecutively from core 0, so a smaller product crowds every rank onto the low chiplets rather than idling cores -- a wrong answer that looks like a valid data point.

images.description: Exactly one of from_make or list.

from_make.description: A libexec/Makefile target such as derecho-hpcg, asked via its echo-<target> rule. One definition of 'the six' rather than a copy that drifts.

name.description: Resolved under /container/app.d/<name> in the image, or an absolute path to a bare executable.

label.description: How this entry is named in job directories and result rows. Defaults to name, and is what distinguishes two entries of the SAME app that differ only in env -- osu_alltoall from osu_allreduce, say.

args.description: Appended to the argv. The app's launch hook is the better place for flags.

env.description: Extra environment for this app's cells, e.g. OSU_BENCHMARK.

placements.description: A placement states only what it ASKS for. What it should get -- L3, NUMA and socket footprint -- follows from the topology probed at job start, so there is no expectation field for a checker to assert against.

omp_variants.description: Defaults to one variant. Crossing two doubles every sweep, and on HPCG the difference measured 2026-08-19 was minor -- opt in per experiment instead.

matrix.description: The axes crossed. Every axis with two or more entries must appear here; bench/validate refuses to drop values silently.

per_job.description: Which of those axes ONE job iterates. The rest become separate jobs. This is the knob that trades queue wait against job length.

profiles.description: Named single cells -- the answer a sweep produced. bench/submit --profile <name> runs only that. bench/collect --emit-profile generates one from results, so the benchmark's output is the production configuration rather than something transcribed by hand.

cluster.description: The machine this runs on. Names sites/<site>/<cluster>.yaml, which supplies the queue, the node geometry and the host-MPI recipe, and sites/<site>/<cluster>/cluster.sh, which supplies the paths and the module bootstrap. It is the CLUSTER, not the site: NCAR is the site, and Derecho and Casper are two clusters of it.
